title: Shopify theme building for Siba Vitamins
description: Siba Vitamins company is a Shopify E-commerce store where I started to learn about web designs, product information, categories, metadata, SEO and, DNS configuration.
body:
Making a change from Network Security and support to build a theme in Shopify was a weird change to be honest but, it was entertaining to start building my carrier and learning about this topic. 

when I started to help my sister with their e-commerce of vitamins and supplements in Shopify. It was a challenge but not difficult...nothing that a IT person can't learn in a few days of burning your eyes with a lot of knowledge. Understanding the basic of how actually Shopify works in *terms of making your on theme* is not that easy even if you use AI. While coding is not my field, I decided to put my knowledge in learning the right prompt for the AI to work on my way without spending much tokens and making a mess. 

If you are getting into AI building with Codex and wants to build a website you need to understand the Shopify Theme Workflow and here I will make a little breakdown: 

**`layout/`-**  The main page framework, including `theme.liquid`. 

**`templates/` -** Page layouts for homepage, products, collections, blog, cart, and search. 

**`sections/`** **\-** Editable page components, such as the header, footer, hero banner, ad featured products. 

**`snippets/ `-** Reusable pieces, such as product cards, prices, and SEO tags.

**`blocks/` -** Smaller components that can be placed inside compatible sections.

**`assets/` -** CSS, JavaScript, logos, images, and font lines. 

**`config/` -** Theme editor settings and their saved values.

**`locales/` -** Translations for buttons, labels, and theme messages. 

Find more info in <https://shopify.dev/docs/storefronts/themes/architecture>

Once you have an idea of this theme directories, your prompt will be easier for the AI to understand your project. However, that does not mean you will copy and paste and that's it...even thought sounds good and we expect the AI to do the work...sadly...the AI will not get it as you think. I will share some of my prompts that helped me to make the theme get builded and thought the time you improve it.  Also Codex or Claude has /skills and /planmode where you give the AI specific task to do. 

#### 1. Plan the theme prompt

Help me plan a custom Shopify theme from scratch for "**brand name**", a store selling "**product type**" to "**target audience**". The visual style should be "**minimal, premium, colorful, natural, etc.**". Use "**colors**" and "**font preferences**".

I need a homepage, product pages, collection pages, a blog, an article page, an About page, a contact page, search, and a cart. Describe the page structure and reusable sections before writing code. Identify which content belongs in the theme and which belongs in Shopify’s database. Ask me about missing information that would materially affect the design. Do not invent product claims, reviews, prices, or business policies.

### 2. Create the theme foundation

Create the foundation of a custom Shopify Online Store 2.0 theme using Liquid, JSON templates, CSS, and JavaScript. Set up the standard theme folders, the main layout, theme settings, translation files, and homepage template. Use clear, maintainable code and Shopify’s current theme conventions. Make colors, typography, spacing, and buttons configurable through the theme editor.

Support mobile and desktop screens, keyboard navigation, and visible focus states. Validate the theme with Shopify Theme Check. Keep the theme unpublished and explain any validation errors.

### 3. Build the homepage

Build the homepage for "**brand name**" using the existing theme foundation. Include these editable sections: announcement bar, header, hero banner, featured collection, image with text, brand benefits, blog articles, and footer. Let me change images, text, buttons, links, and section order in Shopify’s theme editor.

Use real Shopify collections and articles when selected. Use clearly labeled placeholders where content is missing. Preserve a consistent visual style and check the result on desktop and mobile.

### 4. Build the product page

Create a product page for this Shopify theme. Include a media gallery, product title, price, variant selector, quantity field, add-to-cart button, description, collapsible information, and related products. Connect everything to the current Shopify product and selected variant. Handle unavailable variants, sold-out products, and cart errors clearly.

Support app blocks so compatible review apps can be added later. Use product metafields for optional product-specific information. Do not hardcode ingredients, benefits, specifications, or reviews into a template shared by all products.

### 5. Build collection and search

Create collection and search pages that match this theme. Include responsive product cards, pagination, sorting, and Shopify-supported storefront filters. Show the correct product image, title, price, sale price, and availability. Include useful empty states for collections and searches with no results. Keep filter controls accessible and comfortable to use on mobile.

### 6. Add a blog

Build a blog listing template and an article template for this theme. The listing should show featured images, titles, publication dates, excerpts, and pagination. The article should have readable typography, a comfortable content width, proper heading hierarchy, and responsive images. Make optional elements configurable in the theme editor. Use Shopify’s actual blog and article content.

### 7. Add languages 

Prepare the theme for English and Spanish. Put customer-facing interface text in locale files and use Shopify translation keys throughout the theme. Preserve Liquid variables, HTML markup, URLs, and technical identifiers. Allow translated text to wrap without breaking the layout. Explain which content requires separate translation in Shopify, including products, menus, articles, metafields, policies, and app content. 

### 8. Validate and prepare a preview

Review the completed theme and prepare it for an unpublished  Shopify preview. Run Theme Check and test navigation, product variants, **add to cart** behavior, cart updates, search, and forms. Check desktop and mobile layouts. Report what passed, what failed, and anything you could not verify. Package an uploadable theme ZIP with the theme folders at its root. Do not publish it or modify the live theme....end of the prompt.....

Once you copy and edit this, you can also add the `skeleton-theme` in the prompt and it will help a lot. Even tho this prompt looks very complex I guess or very long, took me at least 3 or 4 month to make it this detail or perfect. I share it for however find this blog can use it. I build it four websites so through the time, i improve it little by little.  As a entrepreneur knowledge is our key to succeed in life and getting more information can help us to improve in our carrier or business. This information you can find it anywhere and even the AI will give it to you but sometimes we don't want to read from the AI. Sometimes, we want to read from a human experience and we even feel better when we find someone who it's struggling with a problem same as you and somehow it has the solution...not all the time AI knows all. 

Once you work on this then it comes the hard part...details of the details.... pictures, colors, banners, menu, etc...but it's fine, is part of the journey. While I was working on a theme that was build already, I had to start from scratch to understand the whole process and then begin building (that's how my brain works). I hope this information helps. 

Check the website [www.sibavitamin.com](www.sibavitamin.com) where you will see the final theme build it. By the way, reading and keeping my brain under pressure by learning everyday, you need some supplements. Go there and check their products, you might find interesting products.
